packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 03 - FIRST READING (unverified image reading)

Exposure / process statement
- Nothing in my context gave a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this leaf. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001.jpg to image-026.jpg in /tmp/stams3-read/packet-03. I ran one directory listing of that packet directory to get the image filenames. I opened no other file or directory, used no web or search tool, and did not read packet.json.
- All 26 images loaded. image-001 and image-014 are reduced overviews. image-002 to image-013 are native tiles of the image-001 face (a 4 x 3 grid). image-015 to image-026 are native tiles of the image-014 face (same grid).
- Each face has a modern pencil label in the lower right margin. On image-001/013 it reads "Stams, STA, Frag. 238r", and on image-014/026 it reads "Stams, STA, Frag. 238v". This is a shelfmark written on the leaf, not an identification of the text. I use "238r" and "238v" below only as face labels.
- I did not try to identify the work. Where the ink is stained or blurred I mark the reading uncertain and do not complete it from sense.

Line-labelling convention
Line numbers count down from the first written line of each page in the overview (image-001 or image-014). For each line I give the tiles that show it. Neighbouring tiles overlap, so a line seen in two tiles is the same line, not extra text. Proposed expansions are in parentheses. "?" follows an uncertain reading. Rubricated (red) text is marked [red].

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
- Both faces show one bifolium, or two conjugate leaves, laid open flat. Each face has two pages side by side with a central fold or gutter. The gutter has modern repairs: a translucent tissue patch at the top, a long paper or tissue strip, and a rectangle outlined in grey-blue in the gutter (image-007, 008, 011, 012, 020, 021). Tissue mounting corners sit at all four corners.
- Each page has one column of about 20 lines in a formal gothic textual hand with heavy abbreviation. The ruled frame is visible. The bottom margins are wide and the top margins fairly wide. No running titles are visible.
- Decoration: red rubrics in a smaller script, inline initials touched with red, and two-line painted initials. On 238r these are a red L (left page, line 17), a red Q (right page, line 15) and a blue T (right page, line 19). On 238v they are a red E (left page, line 3), a red H (right page, line 4), a blue I (right page, lines 8 and 16) and a red Q (right page, line 12). One line on the right page of 238r has a faint blue/red flourished initial (line 7).
- Underlining: on 238r, right page, line 9, the words "Et uel-" are underlined in red. On 238v, right page, line 4, the words after the rubric are underlined in red.
- Margins: there are small red marks in the outer right margin of 238r right page at lines 15, 18 and 19 (about "r", "r", "rj"), and of 238r left page at line 16 (red "or"? or "ul"?). There are pale pink ghost letters (a large "I/R" at lines 4-5 and a large "D/Q" at lines 12-13 in the right margin of 238r left page; a "D/O" at about lines 15-16 of 238v left page). These look like offsets of red initials from a facing leaf, not added text.
- 238v: faint brownish mirror-image writing (offset) appears in the lower margins and the gutter of both pages, and there is a large faint offset initial (an L-like shape) under the right page (image-025). I did not read the offsets.
- Damage: dark mould or ink-blot spotting covers much of the right page of 238r (lines 3-17) and the middle of the left page of 238v (lines 3-16). The upper margins are water-stained. There are small holes and a wormhole in the lower margins.
- Tentative interpretation (not an identification): the pages seem to alternate narrative or scriptural-style passages, short prayer-like passages ("Largire nobis domine..."), and passages in an expository register ("typus est", "significat"). Rubrics such as "Ad b. a." and "Dominica v. Secundum lucam" suggest liturgical sequencing. The page order across the bifolium is uncertain.

Selected spans: all four pages, read as fully as the images allow. The areas I could not read are listed under each page and in the limitations.
